messages.subject: Updates on 1.3 from github
messages.body_plain:
I don't know how many people are following the project on github, but I thought I'd post about two important issues:
#10 has some drafts of a vectorization of the API and some profiling data to support the idea that vectorization is important and see the details of what is slowing down R. The idea is to have a vectorized map interface whereby the map can read and write multiple records in one call and efficiently, particularly important for small records.This will be longish treck so I created branch multirec-io
#66 I am developing a script in the comments to this issue for 0-cluster install deployments. The idea is to pack all that's needed in one or few jars, put the content on hdfs, point to that content with the -cachearchive streaming option which causes the jar(s) to be distributed to the nodes and unpacked in the working directory and point to that R for execution on the nodes. Most of the steps are working on our EC2 with some problems in the dynamic libraries department. Fixing that seems possible but making the script into something that works on most platforms without modifications, that's a longer road. That's why I would love to people to try it out as soon as possible on their systems and give feedback. Major premise, you need access to a node that's representative of what's installed on the cluster, same hw and OS.
Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: How to use data in rhbase to make a mapreduce job by rmr
messages.body_plain:
Hello, everyone
I'm a new one in R language & RHadoop.  I've already installed rmr,rhdfs,rhbase packages on my Hadoop & HBase cluster successfully.
Could anyone tell me how to make a mapreduce job by rmr with data in HBase?
I can't find any example about the usage of rmr with rhbase, only with data in HDFS.
I tried to write some test code, but it doesn't work.(detailed in "result.txt")

Make a simple description about my test here...
# new a table named "input" at first
hb.new.table("input", "x", opts=list())

# insert 5 elements in my table
hb.insert("input",list( list(1, c("x"), list(1))))
hb.insert("input",list( list(2, c("x"), list(2))))
...
hb.insert("input",list( list(5, c("x"), list(5))))

# read data from hbase and store them in "small.ints"
small.ints <-hb.scan("input", start=1, colspec=c("x"))

# try an easy map function, I don't know how to give the input argument.
out = mapreduce(input = small.ints, map = function(k,v) keyval(v, v^2))

I guess the data structure returned by HDFS and HBASE is different.
Could anyone tell me how to give a right input (with HBASE data) in mapreduce function?
Thanks for your help!
RHadoop is really an amazing project!

On Sunday, April 8, 2012 7:09:06 AM UTC-7, Celia Wang wrote:
> Hello, everyone
> I'm a new one in R language & RHadoop.  I've already installed rmr,rhdfs,rhbase packages on my Hadoop & HBase cluster successfully.
> Could anyone tell me how to make a mapreduce job by rmr with data in HBase?

It is possible but not easy at this time. Xavier Olive has a proof of concept that it is  possible but you have to jump though some hoops.

> I can't find any example about the usage of rmr with rhbase, only with data in HDFS.
> I tried to write some test code, but it doesn't work.(detailed in "result.txt")
>
> Make a simple description about my test here...

> hb.new.table("input", "x", opts=list())
>
> # insert 5 elements in my table
> hb.insert("input",list( list(1, c("x"), list(1))))
> hb.insert("input",list( list(2, c("x"), list(2))))
> ...
> hb.insert("input",list( list(5, c("x"), list(5))))
>
> # read data from hbase and store them in "small.ints"
> small.ints <-hb.scan("input", start=1, colspec=c("x"))
>
> # try an easy map function, I don't know how to give the input argument.
> out = mapreduce(input = small.ints, map = function(k,v) keyval(v, v^2))
>

This is not supposed to work. Once you do an hb.scan the data is in main memory, so you can process it with a number of R functions but not mapreduce, which works off disk -- hence its ability to deal with big data. The three packages are quite separate and distinct, I think if you mix and match their features like this you are in uncharted territory and you need to know what you are doing. Let's walk before we can run.

> Could anyone tell me how to give a right input (with HBASE data) in mapreduce function?

You can track issue #19 and see what progress Xavier is making. Maybe he could share some details of the proof of concept he's got running.

> Thanks for your help!
> RHadoop is really an amazing project!

Thanks!

Antonio

messages.subject: multiple input tables, replicate joins and choosing keys
messages.subject_clean: multiple input tables, replicate joins and choosing keys
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a problem where the raw input data needs to be mapped to categorical aggregate levels before processing.  The data is medical patient histories, so a natural key would be the patientID.  However, the patient raw data needs to be mapped to various levels of aggregation.  For example, there are over 19,000 antibiotic drugs that match the raw keys to answer the question "did this patient use antibiotics?".  The goal is to compute simple measures of care so most patient histories will have at most a few hundred rows and the processing is of each history is just logical filtering, but messy logical filtering to determine if patient is eligible for a certain type of care and did they receive appropriate care (so return value is a pair of T/F values).  This T/F pairs can then be summarized into a ratio of % of patients with appropriate care.

If I use the patientID as the key, then I potentially need to read the drug table for each patient.  This seems like way too much reading of repeated data.

My questions are:
1) Should I be using RHadoop at all for this? From what I have read of Pig, Pig seems more natural to handle this more complex data flow.
2) Even if the categorical data is small, how can I read these two (actually many different kinds of categories) data streams into 1 rmr process?
3) Does RHadoop have anything like the replicate join in Pig to assist in copying the categories levels to each node?

Thanks

However, the patient raw data needs to be mapped to various levels of aggregation. This T/F pairs can then be summarized into a ratio of % of patients with appropriate care.
>
> If I use the patientID as the key, then I potentially need to read the drug table for each patient.  This seems like way too much reading of repeated data.
>
> My questions are:
> 1) Should I be using RHadoop at all for this? From what I have read of Pig, Pig seems more natural to handle this more complex data flow.

I use RHadoop even to brush teeth in the morning, so maybe I should refrain from answering this one. Just look at the rmr vs pig comparison on kmeans in the tutorial and make up your mind. By the way that's also an example of what you need to do, as the mappers has to combine information about points (big data) and centers (small data), just like raw data and categories in your case.

> 2) Even if the categorical data is small, how can I read these two (actually many different kinds of categories) data streams into 1 rmr process?

Read small data (categories in your case) into a variable in scope for the mapper:

small.data = read.table(file-with-small-data)

mapreduce(input = file-with-big-data, map = function(k,v) {you can access v and small.data here, v is one record of big.data}, ....)

Done

> 3) Does RHadoop have anything like the replicate join in Pig to assist in copying the categories levels to each node?

No, it just does that behind the scenes. It's called abstraction.

You are welcome.

On Monday, April 16, 2012 7:06:26 AM UTC-7, Steve Einbender wrote:
> Hello,
> I'm new to R so I very much appreciate the existence of this community to help me with my learning curve as I transition from SAS to R.

Hi Steve,
 glad to help and your questions are totally pertinent to this for  forum, but learning R and transitioning from SAS are larger issues than we can handle here. A google search [R for SAS users] will return a number of resources, let me be biased in favor of my client here and point to the webinar Introduction to R for SAS and SPSS users <http://www.revolutionanalytics.com/news-events/free-webinars/2011/intro-to-r-for-sas-spss/>, but there are many other relevant documents.

>
> The R program that calls the map and reduce rmr functions(attached) runs successfully, via RStudio, on our distributed Hadoop cluster. I'm trying to interrogate the various function parameters of the map and reduce functions(e.g., fields, k, v v) not only to aid in my learning but, more importantly, to start to implement best practices for debugging.
> I've read the RevolutionAnalytics paper on Debugging rmr Programs which was helpful to implement the debug() function and learn that approach. Of course, this does not work with map and reduce on Hadoop.
> It's unclear to me whether the "local backend" debugging process implies a local instance of Hadoop since map and reduce only work on hdfs..... is this true ?

No, "local" completely sidesteps Hadoop, uses the local file system instead of HDFS and it exists only for learning and  debugging purposes. You can run "local" even if hadoop is not installed.

> More importantly, in the context of the attached code, I don't understand how to implement debugging routines in standalone, pseudo-distributed and distributed modes.

There are significant limitations to debugging in these modes. These are hadoop modes, so  they all correspond to the same backend in rmr, called "hadoop". Which one is selected is outside rmr control and depends on hadoop configuration files. No matter which one is configured, this means that R will rely on hadoop to perform part of the mapreduce call. This implies that the map and reduce function will run inside a different R instance, possibly even on a different machine. The normal debug() function is useless to debug the map and reduce functions. You can still use it up to but not including the map and reduce functions, so there still are uses for it in debugging what happens before and after mapreduce, but not "inside" it so to speak.

> I would greatly appreciate some specific debugging code, relative to the attached code, to help me execute a debugging process.

It's hard to debug a program the purpose of which is unknown to me. I don't see anything obviously wrong with it, other than it is for an outdated version of rmr. The debugging page <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/Debugging-rmr-programs> on the wiki has suggestions on how to debug under both backends, not just local. For short cat(...., file = stderr()) is your best bet. In your program, something like

cat(fields, file = stderr(), sep = ",")

or other variables depending on what you suspect is wrong. Always try with reduced size input first: don't expect to write a TB to stderr and get away with it. If you have to debug on a TB of data because it's the only way to trigger the bug, you can still use cat but you'll have to put inside a condition that is true only for a fraction of the inputs, possibly where you suspect the bug to be triggered.

I hope this helps.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I just installed rhdfs on a datanode and now I am trying to read data
from HDFS.

I can see the files by using hdfs.ls <http://hdfs.ls>("/user/root/data")

I try to retrieve all the files in the /user/root/data folder (ie part-
m-00000, part-m-00001 ...) using x <- hdfs.file("/user/root/data/",
"r")

I get the following error:

Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod",
cl,  :
  java.io.FileNotFoundException: File does not exist: /user/root/data

If I try to retrieve a single file using:
modelfile <- hdfs.file("/user/root/data/part-m-00000", "r")
m <- hdfs.read(modelfile)
model <- unserialize(m)

I get the following error:
Error in unserialize(m) : 'connection' must be a connection

Any help that I can get on both issues would be great.

Rick

keyval(k,as.numeric(v)^2))
